all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] A branch --base now requires merge-base(HEAD, ref); a shallow checkout has none, and the error does not say the clone is shallow. CI with default fetch-depth passing --base origin/main now fails with 'has no merge base with HEAD' instead of a hint to fetch full history (reproduced).

[ADVISORY] 'pre-#175 markers keep matching on their SHA' holds only when main has not advanced; an old --base main marker stored main's tip and no longer matches once main moved. Operators may expect old markers to keep satisfying the gate after upgrade.
[ADVISORY] The internal/baseref import sits inside the stdlib import group. goimports/gci will flag and rewrite it.

[BUG] When a tag and a branch share a short name, rev-parse returns the tag's commit (refs/tags precedes refs/heads) but isBranch is true, so the result is merge-base(HEAD, tag commit) — neither git's answer nor the branch's merge-base; the doc claims git's precedence. A repo with a tag named like a branch reviews against an unexpected base.

[ADVISORY] No test asserts RequestedBase on pr-ready run records (both sites) or the task-done record; deleting the assignments passes every test (mutation-verified). The audit field could silently disappear from pr-ready/task-done runs.jsonl rows.

[ADVISORY] Deleting the '- Requested base:' line from the epic-ready context pack survives go test ./... and the epic-ready shell test (mutation-verified). The epic-ready pack could silently stop naming the base as typed.

[BUG] gitReal flattens every non-zero git exit into a plain error, and the baseref adapter maps every non-timeout error to ok=false. An operational show-ref failure (exit 128: corrupt ref store, permission error) is read as 'not a branch', so baseref resolves the branch name exactly — to its tip — instead of failing. Only git's absent-ref exit (1) should be ok=false; other failures should propagate. On a repo where show-ref fails operationally, --base main silently resolves to main's tip: the reviewed diff includes main's new commits inverted, and gate/record-lenses/fsm init can disagree (fsm gate adapter propagates exit>1). Raised by CodeRabbit on PR #191.

rejected.desc: [ADVISORY] Resolve runs `git rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options`; gitcontext's explicit-base path did not use --end-of-options before. rev-parse accepts it only from git 2.30; older git exits 1 silently under --quiet. On git < 2.30 every explicit --base in review/status/record-lenses fails with a misleading 'invalid git base' (ref is already validated not to start with '-').

[ADVISORY] New InitData field requested_base is written to the audit init event; older binaries decode init with DisallowUnknownFields. Reproduced: a run created by the new binary with --base returns ERR_AUDIT_INVALID from an older binary's fsm state/export in mixed-version setups.

confirmed.desc: [ADVISORY] Deleting the '- Requested base:' line from the epic-ready context pack survives go test ./... and the epic-ready shell test (mutation-verified). The epic-ready pack could silently stop naming the base as typed.

rejected.desc: [ADVISORY] Weakening the shallow condition (shallow != "" or || true) survives; TestUnresolvableBasesFail never asserts the full-clone error omits the shallow hint. A regression would tell users with unrelated histories to fetch full history.
